alignments.note: Supplied copula rides with the verb's own English (rules 7, 9).
Case preposition rides with the pronoun (rule 21).

Genitive relative expanded by the generic noun *things*, which takes the head (rule 77); the *of* realizes the genitive's own case and rides with it, stranded at the end of the English clause and so discontinuous (rules 15, 21), as MAT.6.32 gives the same *of* to ἁπάντων. Reading the *of* as licensed by the English noun *need* and so belonging to χρείαν remains defensible, but rule 21's support-frame exception is scoped to a supplied frame noun over an accusative and does not reach an expressed noun with a genitive complement.
The pair χρείαν ἔχετε spells both its elements out, so it splits like any other (rule 73); the noun keeps a bare *need*.
Nominalizing article of the articular infinitive (rule 61).
Expressed subject of the infinitive takes the English subject word (rule 74).

review_notes: *of* moved from χρείαν to ὧν, reconciling this verse with MAT.6.32, where the identical *have need of* + genitive puts *of* on the genitive. Rule 21's genitive arm decides both; its support-frame exception wants a supplied frame noun over an accusative and neither condition holds here.
The head is unchanged: rule 77 keeps it on the supplied generic noun *things* rather than on the relativizer, and adding the stranded preposition to the unit does not bear on that choice.
χρείαν ἔχετε stays split under rule 73, the ASV spelling both elements out as *have* and *need*; the collapsed arm of that rule is not in question.
